title: Who Did What to Whom: The Passive with Ser

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the passive with *ser* + past participle from B1 Unit 18: *La ley fue aprobada por el Parlamento*. The participle agrees with the subject, and *por* names who did the action. Reports on the dictatorship use it because the people and the institutions that were affected come first.

sections.title: Ser + participle
rows: Miles de personas fueron detenidas sin orden judicial.
La CONADEP fue creada por el presidente Alfonsín.
*fue creada*: singular, feminine; *por* names the agent
Las leyes fueron anuladas por el Congreso en 2003.

items.spanish: Miles de personas fueron detenidas sin orden judicial.
items.english: Thousands of people were detained without a court order.

items.spanish: La CONADEP fue creada por el presidente Alfonsín.
items.english: The CONADEP was created by President Alfonsín.
The former commanders were tried in 1985.

items.spanish: Las leyes fueron anuladas por el Congreso en 2003.
items.english: The laws were annulled by Congress in 2003.

sections.content: Put *ser* in the tense you need (*fue*, *fueron*) and make the participle agree: *creada*, *juzgados*. Add *por* + the agent only when you want to name who did it. If the agent does not matter, you can use the *se* passive, as in *se publican las leyes*.
